delegated_effects: SRand1 and SRand4 consume/update the original 16-bit LFSR seed at DGROUP:8BA2; no RNG state address is directly read or written by SpiderScan. The pinned exact root:0093 helper source and original disassembly show the shared transition seed=(seed<<1) XOR 0x1BF5 only when the shift carries; SRand1 returns unsigned remainder by its range, while SRand4 returns updated seed & 3.

fracCOS, fracSIN, FindAntIndex and DeadAntHere execute as the original helpers in the registered run. Their calls, arguments and ordering are part of the scanner behavior; helper effects are compared at the oracle boundary.

DoLaserFire is a far C call. Its exact argument tuple and event order are compared; the reviewed helper certificate places physical rendering/audio-device effects outside this simulation contract and reports no feedback into RNG, LifeA, ant-list or map state.
memory_state.other_direct_writes: None. On a successful sample SpiderScan returns found; otherwise it returns the initial -1 or the last negative FindAntIndex result. All exits share the far-return epilogue.

constants_widths_pointer_arithmetic.control: dir = ((direction-2)&7)<<5; two passes; each sweep begins at dir-32 and samples while signed a < dir+32, so both sweeps cover 64 angle values.
constants_widths_pointer_arithmetic.sampling: SRand1(12)+1 is a 16-bit int radius in 1..12. The SpiderScan declaration calls the helper through signed int while its pinned definition takes unsigned int; the constant argument is the same ABI word 0x000C, and SRand1 performs unsigned division. Trig returns signed int; it is sign-extended to signed 32-bit long, multiplied by signed long radius, divided with signed truncation toward zero by 32767L, narrowed to 16-bit int, then added to signed 16-bit sx/sy with DOS-word wrap behavior.
constants_widths_pointer_arithmetic.bounds: Signed 16-bit x in [0,127] and y in [0,63] are checked before indexing; each failed predicate branches to the common angle increment. LifeA byte is zero-extended into the 16-bit int life.
constants_widths_pointer_arithmetic.laser: Plane/index selector is 1 for FindAntIndex. Laser endpoint is cell center (x*16+7,y*16+7); first endpoint rereads current raw 16-bit spider coordinates. Kill flag life&0x80 yields only 0 or 128.
constants_widths_pointer_arithmetic.abi: DOS large-model far C calls with 16-bit int/stack arguments; observed caller cleanup is 2, 6, or 8 bytes as applicable. SpiderScan preserves SI/DI, returns int in AX, and exits via RETF. MSC long arithmetic uses signed helper calls; 0x99 instructions at 1000/1006/1016/102F/103D are 16-bit CWD operations, not CDQ (one byte, no 0x66 prefix).
constants_widths_pointer_arithmetic.stack_and_dead_initialization: Original has a 20-byte stack-check request, saves DI then SI, and allocates 10 bytes of locals. found is initialized to -1; pass to 0; local r occupies the [BP-2] home evidenced by its sample assignment at 0FFA and read at 1003. The original zero store to that r home at 0FD4 is dead: direction masking gives dir in 0..224, so initial a=dir-32 is always below dir+32; pass=0 and the first inner-loop condition are both true. SRand1(12)+1 therefore overwrites r at 0FFA before its first read at 1003.

remaining_differences.explanation: The 392-byte original includes a 16-bit zero store into the local r home [BP-2] before the pass loop; the registered 389-byte candidate omits this dead initialization. The value is overwritten by SRand1(12)+1 at 0FFA before its first read at 1003 on every path (pass is set to zero and is therefore <2), so the store has no dataflow to a branch, call, return or memory effect. The registry labels this the historical dead-initialization residue.

review_notes: The registered source and evidence hashes match the behavior manifest. This worker receipt is a review candidate and does not alter or self-admit a frozen claim.

The context listing uses Capstone 5.0.3 and labels the one-byte 16-bit opcode 0x99 as CDQ. Inspection of the selected instruction lengths confirms no 0x66 prefix at the five listed sites; the correct 16-bit operation is CWD. This is a renderer alias, not an original/source semantic difference.

SRand1's prototype in SpiderScan declares a signed int parameter, while the exact root:0093 definition is unsigned int. This scanner passes only constant 12 (word 0x000C), so width, ABI bits and helper result are identical; the helper then performs the documented unsigned remainder. This signature difference is explicitly bounded to this call.

C signed-overflow and negative-right-shift behavior is not portable ISO C. The conclusion is scoped to the pinned MSC 6.00AX DOS build and the registered valid input domain, where the 16-bit wrap, SAR, and signed-long helper behavior are explicit in the original instructions and differential harness.

UI/render and audio-device output in DoLaserFire remains outside this function's simulation contract; its helper identity, exact request arguments and order are accounted, and the helper review documents noninterference with RNG, LifeA, ant-list and map state.

root_review.basis: Reviewed the whole-function branch/call/state/width maps, source/evidence identities, explanations of residue and differential/negative limits. Matching observed service boundaries are composed through the actual caller ABI and same callee/slot/state; finite coverage alone is not acceptance.
